answers.question: Q1
answers.correction: Right in substance: in these 41 papers the identification is a proposal or a candidate from February 2020 on, never derived. Two imprecisions. Minic 2020's abstract states the clause as an implication of the formulation ('implies'); 'proposal' is the word of §6.2, and BHM 2021 §3 repeats that 'proposal' sentence verbatim. Snowmass 2022's 'dark matter should be viewed as a dual SM' is not weaker in wording than 'which we propose'. The record labels it partial because it does not say the dual is the momentum side.

answers.question: Q4
answers.correction: 'No paper says gravity only' is wrong. HM 2024 (2407.06207, §5.3, 'Neutrinos:') says the Berry-phase-like correlation term (cited to BHM 2021) has a mass scale that 'defines the decoupling energy, below which the dark and visible matter interact as required, only gravitationally'. It identifies that scale with M_SM ≈ 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV; recomputed from its Table 1 by scratch/r9-sweep-verify/bin/msm.py, 4.48×10¹⁴ GeV. The family-(a) patterns missed 'only gravitationally'. So one school paper assigns a scale to the coupling, though it does not compute it, and puts every accessible energy in a gravity-only regime. The answer also omits the school's own counterweights to reading the terms as suppressed: 'with a particular double scaling, this term can be finite!' and λ⁸/L¹⁰ 'should not be naively considered to be trans-Planckian' (BHM 2021 §4; BHM 2023 §6.4 likewise); 'the usual visible photon/dark photon coupling is subdominant to this term' (BHM 2021 §5, BHM 2023 §6.5); and the fermion mass gap 'may well be phenomenologically relevant — even for a minuscule numerical value' (BHM 2023 §6.5).

answers.correction:

- FLM 2019's first public date is its publication, 2019-10-10 (print) or 2019-10-15 (online). The Julian Schwinger Centennial talk (Singapore, 7–12 February 2018) is earlier, but the text was not public before October 2019. It is closed access and was not retrieved; see 'retried'.
- BHM 2021 credits 'the explicit appearance of dark matter in the general formulation of string theory' to [14]; EMT 2020's metaparticle candidate cites [50]. Both are composite citations of the whole FLM series, FLM 2019 and Minic 2020 included, so neither dates the identification.
- Outside the 41, FLM's open-access J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 804 (2017) 012032 (online 2017-04-03) has one dark-matter sentence, a pointer with no identification.
- 1601.00662 and 1709.04388 are already in the record's findings.json as precursors; 1801.00160 is not in any record file.

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What their dual is': 'In the foundations it is the momentum side. Freidel, Leigh and Minic 2014 (Phys. Lett. B): … Berglund, Hübsch and Minić 2021 speak of the “canonically conjugate dual space”.'
record_contradictions.note: Checked against the source. In BHM 2021 itself (2010.15610 §2) the coordinates X^A 'combine the sum ( x^{a} ) and the difference ( \mathord{\tilde{x}}_{a} ) of the left- and right-moving chiral bosons on the string', with [x̂, x̂̃] = 2πiλ² (eq. 3). The 'canonically conjugate dual space' sentence follows Tseytlin's leading limit, obtained 'effectively neglecting \omega_{AB} in (2) by assuming that [\hat{x},\mathord{\hat{\tilde{x}}}]=0' (both FOUND). 1905.09463 footnote 4 defines the phrase the same way. So that citation does not support 'the momentum side'. FLM 2014's 'coordinates in momentum space' and x̃ ≡ p/b (Minic 2020 §3, EMT 2021 §2.2, FLM 2016 §1.1, HM 2024 §3.3) do support it. Flag 64 cites only FLM 2014 for the foundations, so the overstatement is in the note's §3 alone.

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'The vacuum': 'The check found no such mechanism in the school's papers, where the classical spacetime label “corresponds to a choice” of polarization'; wiki/phase-space/reciprocity/broken-born-duality.md (description) and wiki/glossary.md: Freidel, Leigh and Minic 'gave no potential and no symmetry-breaking analysis' / 'wrote no potential for it'.
record_contradictions.note:
The quotations are right, and no record file has them: no 'vacuum sector' or 'decoupling frame' in findings.json or panel/C1.evidence.json.
- What the school does say: FKLM 2021 breaks a symmetry 'at the level of the vacuum sector', fixes the decoupling coordinate by 'a choice of ground state', and proposes cosmic expansion as 'a mechanism that selects the decoupling frame'. BHM 2023 §4.3 calls O(1,d−1)₂ 'effectively spontaneously broken'.
- So 'no such mechanism' is too broad if 'such' means any vacuum mechanism that selects which commuting coordinates serve as spacetime. 'No symmetry-breaking analysis' is too broad for FKLM, who include all three FLM authors.
- Where the reader overreaches: 'spontaneous in substance' is its inference. FKLM say the dual symmetry is 'fundamentally broken at the quantum level' because 'the dual Lorentz action is not a canonical transformation', i.e. broken by the λ² bracket. The symmetry is dual Lorentz, not ρ. The coordinates selected (x, x + αx̃ + …) live in the λ²-doubled space. The expansion yields 'a preferred frame' only late, 'as the symmetry is restored as one goes back in time'.
- No potential and no order parameter appear (Goldstone: 0 hits). #11 §3's narrower claim, spontaneous breaking of ρ with η as the order parameter, stands.

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3: 'All nine come from one group and carry one priority, Minic 2020, dated no later than its posting; two earlier items were not read, … a 2019 paper of Freidel, Leigh and Minic not on arXiv'; review/wiki-build-flags.md item 64 quotes Minic 2020's 'metaparticle quanta (the zero modes of the metastring) as the natural quanta of dark matter in this approach'.
record_contradictions.note:
Correct in substance.
- The passages exist: 1709.04388 §5 (2017-09-13) and 1801.00160 §5 (2017-12-30) say metastring or metaparticle quanta may model dark matter, without the dual-of-visible identification. So 'one priority, Minic 2020' holds for the identification but not for the metaparticle clause flag 64 quotes.
- But the record is not unaware. review/literature-check/findings.json already lists 1709.04388 as 'Precursor (2017): the school first suggests that the non-local zero-mode excitations of the metastring (metaparticles, …) can serve as unusual dark-matter quanta for modified dark matter'. It lists 1601.00662 as 'the earliest pointer from the metastring school to dark matter (Jan 2016)'. The inconsistency is between those findings and the wording of the note and the flag.
- 1801.00160 is in no record file.
- On FLM 2019: Minic 2020 §7 also cites it alone ([10]) for dark matter 'represented by metaparticles'. Its first public date is 2019-10-10 (print) or 2019-10-15 (online); February 2018 is the date of the talk, so the reader's '2018–2019' should read October 2019 for the text. It is closed access and was not retrieved.

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3 (plain-language passage): the school's sector 'is correlated with ours by construction, where the program's couples to ours by gravity alone'; 'What differs': 'Their dual sector is correlated with ours by construction'; wiki/summary.md line 34: 'their sector correlated with ours'.
record_contradictions.note:
Correct that BHM 2023 §6.2–§6.3 treat the two sectors as independent to first order in the fundamental length, and that the mixing is invisible in EFT and vanishes as λ → 0 or L → ∞.
- The record does say part of this: note §3 reports the round-1 verifier's finding that the 2021 paper calls the correlation 'invisible in effective field theory, vanishing as λ → 0 or L → ∞'. 'Which the record's wording does not say' is therefore too strong.
- The school does not present the correlation as negligible: 'with a particular double scaling, this term can be finite!' and λ⁸/L¹⁰ 'should not be naively considered to be trans-Planckian' (BHM 2021 §4); 'the usual visible photon/dark photon coupling is subdominant to this term' (BHM 2021 §5, BHM 2023 §6.5); the mass gap 'may well be phenomenologically relevant — even for a minuscule numerical value' (BHM 2023 §6.5); and such a correlation 'has been observed in astronomical data' (BHM 2021 §4). 'Suppressed by powers of λ' is therefore the reader's characterization, not the school's.
- The strongest support for the reader's direction is a passage the reader missed: HM 2024 §5.3, gravity-only coupling below a decoupling energy (next entry).

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What their dual is': 'The identification matches C1 in their foundations; their model doubles phase space where the program polarizes one.'
record_contradictions.note:
The §6.4 passage exists, one section before the §6.5 sentence the record cites, and no record file has it ('canonically conjugate like': no hits).
- It is a heuristic: the authors argue it from the Bohr–Sommerfeld-like form of the λ² mixing term ('This reasoning goes beyond the rules of effective field theory') and say it is 'induced from the domain-space canonical commutation relation between x and {\mathord{\tilde{x}}}', a λ² relation (both FOUND, §6.4). It is a conjugacy of field values inside the doubled model, and the record's 'their model doubles phase space' stays true.
- What changes is the overlap in wording: 'the dual particles are conjugate to the Standard Model particles' is closer to 'conjugate matter' than anything the record quotes.
- A further qualification of 'matches C1 in their foundations': even in EMT 2021 §2.2, where x̃ ≡ p/b, the dual fields come from 'the dual momenta p and \tilde{p} (to x and \tilde{x} respectively)', i.e. from the doubled phase space.

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3: 'Their dual sector is correlated with ours by construction' versus the program's coupling 'by gravity alone'; review/wiki-build-flags.md item 64: 'Their dual sector is correlated with ours; #11's couples by gravity alone under strict P4 (row 7)'; wiki/summary.md line 34: 'their sector correlated with ours'.
record_contradictions.note:
Found by this verification, not by the reader.
- HM 2024 (2407.06207, posted 2024-07-03, before P.R.'s September 2026 notebook), §5.3 'Neutrinos:': dark and visible matter 'mix via a Berry phase-like correlation term[103]. The mass-scale of this correlation term defines the decoupling energy, below which the dark and visible matter interact as required, only gravitationally.' M_SM ≈ 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV is 'naturally identifiable with this dark-matter/visible-matter decoupling scale' (both FOUND). Recomputed from its Table 1 by scratch/r9-sweep-verify/bin/msm.py: 4.48×10¹⁴ GeV.
- So one prior paper of the school states, for all energies below ~10¹⁴ GeV, a coupling by gravity alone, which matches the program's P4 at accessible energies.
- The contrast 'correlated with ours … where the program's couples by gravity alone' holds against BHM 2021 and BHM 2023 (a correlated dual photon, a dual Z, accelerator events) but not against HM 2024. The school is not consistent on the point, and the summary's clause understates the overlap.
- No record file has the passage ('decoupling energy', 'interact as required': no hits).

missed.quote: The mass-scale of this correlation term defines the decoupling energy, below which the dark and visible matter interact as required, only gravitationally.
missed.why_it_matters: The school's own statement of gravity-only coupling. Below a decoupling energy that HM identify with M_SM ≈ 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV (4.48×10¹⁴ GeV from their Table 1, by code), dark and visible matter interact only gravitationally. It refutes the reader's Q4 'No paper says gravity only', which its family-(a) patterns missed, qualifies Q5, and weakens the record's contrast 'correlated with ours … where the program's couples by gravity alone'. Posted 2024-07-03, so prior art; in no record file.

missed.quote: Note that with a particular double scaling, this term can be finite!
missed.where: §4, immediately after eq. (19) and the 'vanishes as either λ → 0 or L → ∞' sentence
missed.why_it_matters: Both the reader and the record quote the vanishing limit; the authors qualify it in the very next sentence.

missed.quote: However, the ratio \frac{\lambda^{8}}{L^{10}} should not be naively considered to be trans-Planckian
missed.why_it_matters: The school warns against reading the mixing as negligible; the reader's record contradiction 4 calls the terms 'suppressed'. BHM 2023 §6.4 repeats it for λ₄²/L⁴.

missed.quote: Such a correlation between visible and dark matter involving an IR scale (in this case, the Hubble scale) has been observed in astronomical data and has been studied in the context of modified dark matter in [18].
missed.why_it_matters: The authors present the visible–dark correlation as already observed (the MDM acceleration scale), not as an unobservable sub-leading term.

missed.quote: Also, the usual visible photon/dark photon coupling is subdominant to this term that is inherent in our story.
missed.why_it_matters: The school holds its non-gravitational correlation to dominate ordinary kinetic mixing, in contrast with #11 P4's ε ≲ 10⁻¹³. BHM 2023 §6.5 repeats it. It contradicts HM 2024 §5.3 (above).

missed.quote: may well be phenomenologically relevant — even for a minuscule numerical value of
missed.why_it_matters: A further counterweight to 'suppressed': the authors say the mass gap can be visible even when the mixing is tiny.

missed.quote: The dual momenta p and \tilde{p} (to x and \tilde{x} respectively) lead, via the canonical minimal-coupling prescription, not only to the usual fields \phi but also to their duals \tilde{\phi} (see below).
missed.where: §2.2, the section that defines x̃ ≡ p/b
missed.why_it_matters: Even in the 'foundations' presentation, where x̃ is rescaled momentum at ℏ, the dual (dark) fields come from p̃, the momentum conjugate to x̃: the doubled phase space. This narrows the record's 'The identification matches C1 in their foundations'.

missed.quote: Thus we have “dark matter” fields, \tilde{\phi}(x) , in the effective classical spacetime x description (after integrating over the dual spacetime \tilde{x} ).
missed.where: §3.3, after 'If we turn on backgrounds' p → p+φ, p̃ → p̃+φ̃
missed.why_it_matters: HM 2024 makes the same move: the dark fields are background shifts of the metaparticle's dual momentum p̃, after the λ²-conjugate x̃ is integrated out, not the x̃ ≡ p/ε of the same section.

missed.quote: It should be clear though that there is nothing special about the x^{\mu} ; we could have taken any linear subspace, such as \tilde{x},p .
missed.why_it_matters: In the founding metaparticle paper, spacetime is a choice of Lagrangian subspace and any other would do: the other polarization is equally lawful, as in #11 P5.

missed.quote: the space-time on which the metaparticle propagates is ambiguous, with different choices related by what in string theory we would call T-duality
missed.why_it_matters: No selection mechanism; the alternative spacetimes are equivalent under T-duality.

missed.quote: We stress that there are really two ways in which we can extend the cell[245]: either we extensify modular space along the space directions or the dual space directions.
missed.why_it_matters: Classical space emerges by extensifying along the space directions, and the school names the dual directions as the other option. The choice is posed, not explained (Q9).

missed.quote: In other words the dual Lorentz action is not a canonical transformation.
missed.why_it_matters: FKLM's own reason the dual symmetry is broken: it does not preserve the λ² bracket. This is a breaking by the symplectic structure, and it weighs against the reader's reading of the vacuum-sector breaking as 'spontaneous in substance'.

missed.quote: the expansion of the Universe gives rise to a preferred frame and the infrared Lorentz violation appears only for an old Universe, as the symmetry is restored as one goes back in time
missed.why_it_matters: The expansion mechanism selects a frame only at late times, in the cosmological frame; earlier the symmetry is restored. Bears on Q9 and on the record's 'no such mechanism'.

missed.quote: We see that although p,\tilde{p} might resemble a doubling of momentum space, the propagator contains a simple pole along with a \delta -function constraint.
missed.why_it_matters: FKLM caution that (p, p̃) only resembles a doubled momentum space. This bears on how far the record's 'their model doubles phase space' goes.

missed.quote: We now make use of the fact that the metaparticle couples to the extended metric (3)
missed.why_it_matters: FKLM's candidates gravitate through the extended Born metric (g on x, g⁻¹ on x̃), which is why the dual momenta redshift oppositely (eq. 16). Qualifies Q6's 'gravitates on the observed metric'.

missed.quote: Note also that our G_{N} could vary by varying the volume of the dual spacetime.
missed.why_it_matters: G_N is tied to the dual-space volume and may vary with it; an addition to Q6.

missed.quote: dark matter correlated to visible matter and dark energy [12] and represented by metaparticles [10]
missed.where: §7 (Conclusion); [10] = Freidel, Leigh, Minic, Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 34 (2019) 1941004
missed.why_it_matters: Minic 2020 cites the unread, non-arXiv FLM 2019 paper alone for dark matter represented by metaparticles. With BHM 2023 §4.3's [254], it is the second single citation of that paper in a dark-matter context (Q11, flag 64).

missed.quote: The proposal here is that the dual sector (as already indicated in the previous section) should be interpreted as the dark matter sector, which is correlated to the visible sector via the dark energy sector, as discussed in [18].
missed.why_it_matters: The record's second anchor paper repeats Minic 2020 §6.2's sentence verbatim, so in BHM 2021 too the identification is called a 'proposal'. Its 'correlated' runs 'via the dark energy sector' (MDM, [18]), not through an interaction term.

missed.quote: This reasoning goes beyond the rules of effective field theory.
missed.where: §6.4, between 'First the fields and their duals are “canonically conjugate” like q and p' and 'the dual particles are conjugate to the Standard Model particles'
missed.why_it_matters: Marks the field-space conjugacy (the reader's contradiction 5) as a heuristic argued from the Bohr–Sommerfeld-like form of the mixing term. The same paragraph says it is 'induced from the domain-space canonical commutation relation between x and x̃', a λ² relation (code-checked: FOUND).

missed.quote: Being simply laced, E_{8}^{\vee}\approx E_{8} , and they are physically indistinguishable.
missed.why_it_matters: The 'electro-magnetic dual' of the record's C4 reading is a pairing of two gauge groups that the authors call physically indistinguishable; nothing magnetically charged is involved.

missed.quote: which halves the spacetime akin to the quantum-mechanical restriction of the classical phase space, (p,q) , in the coordinate or momentum representation
missed.why_it_matters: The school likens choosing half of the λ²-doubled space to choosing the coordinate or momentum representation of (p, q), 'or indeed any other' polarization: the program's language, applied to the doubled space.

missed.quote: The indeterminacies \delta p and \delta\tilde{p} thereby being interchangeable provides the first substitution in the chain
missed.where: §2.4, the 'more elementary' argument for modular spacetime
missed.why_it_matters: Here the dual coordinate q̃ is introduced through the dual momentum p̃, and its l_P² conjugacy to q comes from combining quantum indeterminacy with the Schwarzschild radius. The 'dual' is a gravitationally motivated doubled coordinate, not the momentum at ℏ.

retried: FLM 2019: Freidel, Leigh and Minic, 'Manifest non-locality in quantum mechanics, quantum field theory and quantum gravity', Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 34 (2019) 1941004 (INSPIRE recid 1760046; DOI 10.1142/S0217751X19410045; also the book chapter DOI 10.1142/9789811213144_0004, Proceedings of the Julian Schwinger Centennial Conference (JS100), Singapore, 7–12 February 2018). This is the reader's lead; it was not read. Not retrieved on the second attempt either. Unpaywall and OpenAlex report both DOIs closed ('oa_status': 'closed', no repository copy, any_repository_has_fulltext false). The World Scientific article page returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, the Semantic Scholar API answered 429 twice, and a web search found no copy. First public date: published 2019-10-10 (print) and 2019-10-15 (online) per Crossref, i.e. before Minic 2020 (2020-02-29). The INSPIRE and Crossref abstract mentions 'the new concept of metaparticles inherent to such an effective non-commutative description in terms of bi-local quantum fields', not dark matter. It is cited alone in a dark-matter context twice, by Minic 2020 §7 ([10]) and BHM 2023 §4.3 ([254], with Minic 2020). Its full text is still the one source that could move the identification's priority before February 2020.

Side find, outside the 41 papers: Freidel, Leigh and Minic, 'Modular Spacetime and Metastring Theory', J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 804 (2017) 012032 (ISQS conference; not on arXiv; CC-BY gold open access per Unpaywall; online 2017-04-03 per Crossref). curl on IOP's PDF URL returned a Radware bot-check page, which was not bypassed. WebFetch, the route the brief allows, then received the PDF normally; it was read with pypdf (scratch/r9-sweep-verify/dl/jpcs804/flm2017_jpcs.txt, 21 pages). Its only dark-matter mention: 'Finally, we think that there are implications of the metastring for the problems of dark matter and the origin of the standard model of particle physics or the physics of the early universe.' This is a pointer by the three FLM authors with no identification, so it changes no priority. It does qualify the record's findings.json remark (for 2104.00802) that the FLM 'core papers of 2013–2019 never mention dark matter', if this conference review counts as a core paper.
overall: The reader's output can be relied on for its quotations: all 163 were found verbatim, and the 41 first-posted dates and the sweep counts reproduce under independent code. Most readings also hold; 11 need corrections and one is refuted (a misidentified reference). The serious gap is a missed passage. HM 2024 §5.3 states that below a decoupling energy of about 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV the school's dark and visible matter interact 'only gravitationally'; this refutes the reader's 'no paper says gravity only' and weakens the summary's contrast between 'correlated with ours' and gravity alone. The reader's record contradictions are right in substance, but several are overstated: the record's findings.json already holds the 2016–2017 precursors and the a·ã analogy, and the school does not treat its correlation as negligible.
